name: Disease with Focal Palmoplantar Keratoderma as a Major Feature

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Focal Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated, focal hyperkeratotic plaques localized to the palms and/or soles
Histopathological confirmation showing epidermal hyperplasia with orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
Exclusion of other hereditary or acquired palmoplantar keratodermas by clinical and genetic testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of focal palmoplantar keratoderma plaques confirmed by histopathology and exclusion of other keratoderma types
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist in differential diagnosis but is not definitive for all cases.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal well-demarcated hyperkeratotic plaques on palms
searchTerms: raised thick skin areas on palms

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal well-demarcated hyperkeratotic plaques on soles
searchTerms: raised thick skin areas on feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized thickening of the stratum corneum in affected palmoplantar areas
searchTerms: thickened outer skin layer on palms and soles
skin thickening on hands and feet
mild cracks within thickened skin plaques
small skin splits in thick plaques
intermittent skin redness near scaly spots

common.symptomName: Pruritus localized to affected palmoplantar areas
searchTerms: localized itching on hands and feet

common.symptomName: Pain or discomfort on pressure over hyperkeratotic plaques

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of fissured plaques
Nail dystrophy associated with adjacent keratoderma

searchTerms: excessive sweating on hands and feet
overactive sweat glands in hands and feet

rare.symptomName: Development of painful callosities leading to gait disturbance
searchTerms: painful thickened skin causing walking problems

rare.symptomName: Associated mild palmoplantar hyperhidrosis with malodor
searchTerms: excessive sweating and odor on palms and soles
mild palm and sole sweating with smell
hyperhidrosis with malodor on hands and feet

rare.symptomName: Secondary fungal infections in affected areas

laboratory: Histopathology showing epidermal hyperplasia with orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
Negative fungal cultures in primary lesions
imaging: Not typically required; imaging may be used to assess secondary musculoskeletal complications
genetic: Possible mutations in keratin genes (e.g., KRT9, KRT1) in some familial cases
Genetic testing useful for differential diagnosis
other: Clinical examination revealing sharply demarcated focal plaques on palms and soles

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse rather than focal involvement of palms and soles
Multiple small hyperkeratotic papules rather than large plaques
Onset in adulthood with possible underlying systemic disease
Resolution upon treatment of underlying cause

redFlags: Presence of systemic symptoms such as weight loss or fever
Development of ulceration or non-healing fissures
references: Orphanet: Disease with focal palmoplantar keratoderma as a major feature, ORPHA:307871
